subject: Luminex demo: pilot candidate slate and alignment note
messages:
From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Anya Petrov <anya@luminex.ai>, Michael Patel <michael@luminex.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Luminex demo: pilot candidate slate and alignment note

Hi Anya / Michael —

Thanks again for the demo earlier. Wanted to capture a concise recap and our recommended next moves so we don’t lose momentum. Below is a short synthesis plus asks and links to the artifacts we referenced.

Quick recap (what we heard)
- Primary goal: ship an in-product summarization and RAG-backed assistant for enterprise users with <200ms median token latency targets for short replies, and 99th percentile SLOs <1.2s for non-streaming paths.
- Data profile: mixed short-to-mid length prompts with domain-specific terminology (legal/insurance). Accuracy and hallucination control are higher priority than absolute cost, but unit-cost sensitivity matters once we scale to ~200k qpm tokens/month.
- Security/controls: must run within customer VPC (Private) for pilot and require audit logs + KMS.

Recommended pilot candidate slate (ops-minded shortlist + rationale)
1) redwood-rt-medium-quant (recommended pilot default) — Best balance: 15–25% lower token cost vs standard fp16 engines with modest quality delta on summarization; observed median latency improvements (~12%) on our 1k prompt sample. Good fit if latency/cost are gating.
2) open-instruct-large-8q (fallback for highest-quality responses) — Higher cost but consistently better faithfulness on long-form context (docs >2k tokens). Useful as a selective fallback for the RAG/grounded path.
3) legacy-llama-2-13B (cheap baseline for non-critical batch jobs) — Lowest unit cost for background enrichment steps; avoid for user-facing summary generation.

Key tradeoffs and ops notes
- Cost vs quality: our bench shows redwood-rt-medium-quant is ~0.18$/1k tokens vs open-instruct-large-8q ~0.45$/1k tokens for comparable prompt sets. We recommend starting pilot with mixed routing (default to redwood-rt-medium-quant; route to open-instruct-large-8q when confidence score < 0.6 or when chain-of-thought retrieval hits >1 doc).
- Latency: redwood-rt-medium-quant hits median 110–130ms on our staging GPUs for the sample set; open-instruct-large-8q median is ~240ms (non-stream). We recommend keeping a 200ms fallback policy for interactive flows.
- Regression guardrails: include a small regression suite (10–15 prompts) we should run nightly — see attached prompt set (luminex_prompt_set_v2.jsonl) and the benchmark summary.

Attachments and links
- Attached: redwood_benchmark_summary_v1.csv (sample-level cost/latency/qa metrics), luminex_prompt_set_v2.jsonl (pilot prompt pack), pilot_cost_model_v1.xlsx (monthly/peak cost projections).
- Benchmarks and runbook: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/1A2b3BenchmarkPack

Asks / next steps
- Anya: confirm internal pilot stakeholders and that VPC requirements are feasible for an initial 30-day pilot.
- Michael: please send the standard security questionnaire items we need to validate (we flagged KMS + audit log access).
- Internal (Marissa/Ben): prep a quick MVP routing config (canary to 50 users) and a regression alerting rule for hallucination rate >2% on the prompt pack.

Proposed timeline
- This week: finalize pilot routing slate + gating prompts (we can iterate Friday).
- Week of Nov 29: provision private pilot, run smoke benchmarks, initial 7-day pilot.

I’m available to jump on a quick call to finalize the mutual action plan — suggested 30-min slot tomorrow 10–10:30 PT if that works.

Thanks,
Grace O'Connor

Thanks Grace — really helpful summary. A few quick clarifying questions from our side: 

1) Regression concern: we saw edge hallucinations in the demo when the prompt mixed contract clauses + out-of-scope policy language. Can you call out which of the candidate engines had the lowest hallucination rate on the edge-case prompt subset? We need that for our internal risk review.

2) Fallback policy: if redwood-rt-medium-quant is default, what’s the expected switch-over latency to open-instruct-large-8q for the same request (i.e., when a request is re-routed after low confidence)?

3) Security: our infra leads will want to validate whether private pilot requires customer-managed KMS or if Redwood can integrate with our existing KMS through a connector — we'll share the SOC teammate who will coordinate.

We can do the 30-min slot tomorrow; 10–10:30 PT works for Michael. Please include Ben for the commercial questions.

Best,
Anya
Head of Product, Luminex AI
anya@luminex.ai

Grace — looping in operational notes and answers to Anya's questions so we have something to present on the call.

On hallucination rates
- Short answer: open-instruct-large-8q had the lowest hallucination rate on the edge-case subset (~0.9% hallucination on our labeled 250-sample legal-edge set). redwood-rt-medium-quant is at ~1.8% on the same set — still within acceptable pilot tolerances but double the high-quality engine.

Switch-over latency (route to fallback)
- Measured end-to-end: 1) detection (confidence calc) ~12–18ms, 2) routing decision/read-through negligible, 3) cold start to open-instruct-large-8q if model instance not warm ~210–260ms; warm instance median ~120–150ms. Recommend warm pool for fallback to keep user-visible latency <300ms when fallbacks occur.

Cost/ops notes
- Pilot cost model attached (pilot_cost_model_v1.xlsx). Under a 30-day pilot with ~800k tokens/day, expected incremental hosted cost (Redwood-hosted pilot) ranges $3.5k–$7.5k depending on dynamic routing thresholds. For Private pilot costs, the main delta will be infra provisioning and network egress if cross-VPC — we'll need Luminex infra input.

Proposed guardrails and alerts
- Nightly regression run (15 prompts) with automated diff against baseline; alert if hallucination delta >0.5% absolute or if latency P95 moves >200ms.
- Canary routing: 5% -> 25% -> 50% over 72 hours with health checks on accuracy + latency.

I attached the benchmark CSV + prompt pack used to compute the numbers. Happy to run a quick pre-meeting dry-run.

Marissa Cole
Product Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
